=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_non_retryable_backfill.sh: PR listing loop, `orderBy: {field: UPDATED_AT, direction: ASC}` with `while [ "${fetched}" -lt "${MAX_PRS}" ] | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: Each tick starts from the first page and reads at most `MAX_PRS` (default 50) of the least recently updated open PRs. Idle PRs that have no non-retryable marker stay in that window on every tick. Only a PR that gets a new comment, such as the backfill marker, moves to the back. The `reason=listing_truncated` warning shows the cut-off but does not advance past it.
  WHY: Once more than `MAX_PRS` idle, ineligible PRs sit ahead of a stuck PR in `UPDATED_AT ASC` order, every tick reads the same window. A stuck PR beyond the window never gets its diagnosis. The setting is capped at 200 and the cut-off is logged, so I rate this a NIT.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_non_retryable_backfill.sh: `bounded_int()` and `page_size=$((MAX_PRS - fetched))` in the PR listing loop | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: `bounded_int` accepts `^[0-9]{1,6}$`, so a value with a leading zero such as `08` passes. The `[ ... -lt ... ]` tests treat it as decimal, but the bash `$(( ))` expansion reads it as invalid octal.
  WHY: With `WORKFLOW_HEAL_NON_RETRYABLE_BACKFILL_MAX_PRS=08` (an operator-set repo variable), `page_size` is not computed. The first listing call then gets an empty `first=` argument and fails, so the tick ends in `pr_listing_unavailable`. The header comment says every exit is 0 and invalid values fall back to the default. This is a bad configuration that silently disables the pass, which is why it is a NIT.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_non_retryable_backfill.sh: `live_head` read via the `python3 -I -B -c` snippet, followed by `if [ "${live_head}" != "${head}" ]` that logs `reason=head_moved` | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: A successful PR read whose JSON has no readable `head.sha`, or whose parse fails, leaves `live_head` empty. That case is logged as `head_moved`.
  WHY: An unreadable payload and a real push both log `reason=head_moved`. Operators cannot tell them apart, although only the first is a transient or API fault.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml: step "Backfill non-retryable autofix failure reports" (env block). The sibling steps at lines 203 and 581 pass `HEAD_REF_FILTER: ${{ inputs.head_ref_filter }}`. | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The enumerate and CI-rerun steps honor the `head_ref_filter` dispatch input, but the new step neither receives it nor filters by it. The driver has no filter.
  WHY: An operator who dispatches the sweep with `head_ref_filter=claude/` and `dry_run=false` to limit the blast radius still gets an unfiltered backfill. It scans all open PRs and can dispatch reports and post marker comments on PRs outside the filter, and the intake then adds `ai:needs-human` to them. The step is capped at 3 dispatches per tick and runs as a manual-dispatch case only, so I rate it a NIT.
- Requirement: unattended_system_instructions.md §20.E-F say a new recurring script or supervisor wired into a scheduler needs an entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`, with script path, introduction PR, type, removal trigger, removal preflight checks and owner.
  Expected change site: docs/scripts-pending-removal.md. Either add an entry for scripts/workflow_failure_heal_non_retryable_backfill.sh or extend the existing heal-family entry at line 69, which lists only workflow_failure_heal_report.sh, workflow_failure_heal_autofix_report.sh, workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh and workflow_failure_heal.py.
  Evidence of absence: The PR's changed-file list does not include docs/scripts-pending-removal.md. I grepped that file and it has no reference to the new script. Other scheduled helpers such as scripts/workflow_retro.py (line 117) and scripts/assemble_changelog.py (line 222) have entries, which gives precedent for scheduled scripts. If maintainers read §20.F as covering only standalone or long-running scripts, this drops to NIT.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_non_retryable_backfill.sh: lines 155-159 (the PR listing loop) and line 179 (resetting cursor) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The PR listing cursor is reset to empty at the start of every tick, and the loop processes PRs starting from the oldest updated.
  WHY: If the repository has more open PRs than `MAX_PRS` (default 50), the backfill will always scan the same oldest-updated PRs. If those PRs are ineligible (e.g., cross-repository, or lack a trusted marker), the script will process them in every tick and terminate without reaching PRs beyond the `MAX_PRS` window. Eligible failures beyond the first 50 PRs will never be diagnosed.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_non_retryable_backfill.sh: line 70, `bounded_int()` function | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The validator accepts leading-zero values such as `08` and `09`.
  WHY: Bash arithmetic `$(( ... ))` (implicitly used by the `-lt` comparison) interprets numbers starting with `0` as octal. `08` and `09` are invalid octal values, causing a syntax error. Because `set -u` is enabled, this syntax error terminates the script non-zero, violating the "every exit is 0" contract stated in the helper's header.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml: lines 543-563 (the "Backfill non-retryable autofix failure reports" step) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The new step does not accept or apply the `head_ref_filter` (or any equivalent) that other sweep-based steps respect.
  WHY: An operator who intends to limit the blast radius by dispatching the sweep with a filter will find that this backfill step ignores the filter, performing an unfiltered scan that can dispatch reports, post marker comments, and add `ai:needs-human` labels to PRs outside the intended scope.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_non_retryable_backfill.sh: line 66 (the reporter path assignment) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: `WORKFLOW_HEAL_AUTOFIX_REPORT_SH` is configurable via environment without GATING, allowing the backfill to execute a caller-provided script with the backfill's environment (including `GH_PAT`).
  WHY: While currently unset in workflows, an override of this variable would allow arbitrary execution, bypassing intended security boundaries.
- Requirement: unattended_system_instructions.md §20.E-F say a new recurring script wired into a scheduler gets an entry in docs/scripts-pending-removal.md, including script path, introduction PR, type, removal trigger, preflight checks and owner.
  Expected change site: docs/scripts-pending-removal.md
  Evidence of absence: The PR's changed files do not include docs/scripts-pending-removal.md, and it contains no reference to the new script `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_non_retryable_backfill.sh`.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

  PROBLEM: bounded_int accepts leading-zero numeric strings such as "08" because the regex check `^[0-9]{1,6}$` matches them, but bash interprets "08" as invalid octal in `$((MAX_PRS - fetched)`.
  WHY: a single-digit-per-position override fails the entire backfill without a distinct error reason, so the operator sees `pr_listing_unavailable` and assumes GitHub-side trouble when the trigger is local config.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_non_retryable_backfill.sh: 302-311 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The new head-binding python wrapper handles every failure mode with `|| true`. If `gh api ... /pulls/<n>` succeeded but `head.sha` is missing, the response is not a dict, or json.load itself crashed, `live_head` is empty and the script logs `reason=head_moved` — conflating three distinct failure modes (real head change, malformed payload, wrapper crash) into one operator-visible reason. A genuine GitHub API anomaly would be hidden behind a "head moved" tag whose remediation is to wait, not to investigate.
  WHY: operators cannot distinguish a transient API issue from a real head push; both skip the candidate, but only the push case actually needs waiting.
